source_doctrine: carr-workspace-bduf section s01a 'Operating objective and AI-session displacement test'
doctrine_rule: Before implementation, instrument or interview the following measures. Do not invent a baseline. Store the evidence method, observation window, result, bound product action, and post-launch comparison for each measure.
register_rule: carr-workspace-bduf s27 and carr-control-room-bduf s34: the register must name the method, owner, and observation window rather than fabricate a value.
baseline_context: These measure the CURRENT world, before CARR Workspace and CARR Control Room ship. Tasks are performed with the partner's existing tools, never against the Phase 0 prototypes. Timing a partner on the prototypes would measure the proposed system rather than the baseline it is supposed to beat, and would make the post-launch comparison meaningless.

measures.measure: Joe's current weekly time spent using heavy AI sessions for routine system or business operation
measures.method_detail: Derive from local session records; classify sessions as routine-operation versus exploration/construction, since doctrine objective 8 permits heavy sessions for exploring, investigating genuinely complex problems, and constructing something new. Only routine-operation time counts against this baseline.
measures.bound_product_action: Prioritize product controls and Doc routes for the largest measured categories.
measures.post_launch_comparison: Remeasure weekly time on the same basis.

measures.measure: Count and categories of routine questions that require Claude Code or Codex explanation
measures.method_detail: Classify question-shaped turns in session transcripts. Joe validates the category scheme once; he does not supply the count.
measures.bound_product_action: Add the missing visual explanation or qualified Doc answer route.
measures.post_launch_comparison: Recount by the same categories and observation window.

measures.measure: Count and categories of recurring actions that cannot be completed visually
measures.method_detail: System derives a candidate list from verb-call frequency over the window; Joe confirms which genuinely had no visual route.
measures.bound_product_action: Prioritize the corresponding straightforward control or exact action card.
measures.post_launch_comparison: Recount the remaining non-visual routines by category.

measures.measure: Median time to determine business state and system health
measures.method_detail: This measure CANNOT be instrumented: it measures human comprehension time, not system activity. Six tasks, three business-state and three system-health, issued one at a time. The proctor records send time and answer time; elapsed time is the measurement. No hint is given about where to look, matching the uncoached journey discipline. Every answer is independently verified against the record afterward, because a fast wrong answer is not a fast answer.
measures.known_bias: Elapsed time includes reading the question and typing the answer, neither of which occurs in a silent real workflow. The bias is accepted and held CONSTANT: the post-launch remeasure uses the identical six tasks and the identical send-to-answer method, so the comparison remains valid even though the absolute number is inflated.

tasks.prompt: How many deals are active right now, and which single one needs you first?
tasks.ground_truth: deal-board returns 65 deal rows. 4 are closed, so 61 are not-closed. By phase: pending 23, research 14, negotiation 9, legal 6, due_diligence 5, closing 1, closed 4. THE QUESTION HAS NO SINGLE DEFENSIBLE ANSWER FROM THE BOARD, WHICH IS ITSELF A FINDING: 'active' can mean not-closed (61) or past-pending and actually in motion (38). The board offers no active flag and no definition, so any answer requires the partner to supply one. On the second half, deals whose lead_owner is joe are Drew Knight (pending, last touch 2026-06-10), Terence Cooper (pending, 2026-02-27), Randy Ramsey (research, no touch), Erik Petersen (negotiation, 2026-08-05), Gulf Coast Pelvic Health (legal, 2026-07-30). The strongest candidate for needs-you-first is Gulf Coast Pelvic Health: furthest advanced of Joe's deals at legal phase, and silent 14 days. Erik Petersen is the runner-up at negotiation and 8 days silent. ACCEPTABLE ANSWERS: any count with a stated definition of active, plus Gulf Coast Pelvic Health or Erik Petersen named with a reason.
tasks.measurement_note: First issue at 2026-08-12T21:08:34-05:00 was VOIDED: the partner stepped away and the elapsed time would have measured the break rather than the task. Second issue at 2026-08-13T08:45:53-05:00 was disrupted by a conduct gate holding the proctor's turn. Clock restarted cleanly on the third issue; only the final elapsed time is recorded.

tasks.answer_verbatim: i have 44 deals / nothing is listed in 'needs attention' so I'd say probably blair stiles needs to be followed up on negotiations
tasks.correctness: answered fast, both halves diverge from the record
tasks.finding_1_count_does_not_reconcile: Joe's working number is 44. deal-board returns 65 rows, 61 not-closed, 38 past-pending. 44 matches none of them. Neither number can be called wrong without knowing his source, which is itself the finding: the count he operates from does not reconcile with the record layer, and nothing on either surface reveals the divergence.
tasks.finding_2_false_negative_on_needs_attent: THE MOST DAMAGING RESULT IN THIS MEASURE. Joe reported 'nothing is listed in needs attention'. The record layer's stale-records returns FIFTY-SIX stale deals at that same moment, including Terence Cooper at 167 days quiet, Tyler Gregory at 71, Drew Knight at 64, Jeffrey Yee at 57, Elizabeth Hughes at 22 and James Allen Tyrer at 15. The surface told the partner there was nothing to attend to while 56 deals sat stale.
tasks.finding_3_mechanism: Fifty of those 56 carry last_touch null and days_quiet null — no touch data captured at all. A needs-attention view that filters on days_quiet therefore excludes them for being null rather than for being healthy, so absence of data renders as absence of problems. The stale-records verb warns of exactly this in its own description: 'Empty can mean nothing stale OR nothing captured.' Silence is being read as health, and this is the concrete case the Command Center overview must fix.
tasks.finding_4_ownership: Blair Stiles is genuinely stale (last_touch null) so the instinct was sound, but its lead_owner is dell, not joe. The question asked which deal needs JOE first. The Joe-owned candidates were Gulf Coast Pelvic Health (legal phase, 14 days silent) and Erik Petersen (negotiation, 8 days). Nothing on the surface he used distinguishes his deals from Dell's at a glance.

tasks.prompt: Which client or lead has gone longest without a touch?
tasks.ground_truth: THE LONGEST MEASURABLE is Terence Cooper at 167 days quiet (last touch 2026-02-27), a Joe-owned deal. Next are Tyler Gregory 71 days, Drew Knight 64, Jeffrey Yee 57, Elizabeth Hughes 22, James Allen Tyrer 15. BUT THE TRUE ANSWER IS UNKNOWABLE FROM THE RECORD, and that is the finding: 50 of the 56 stale deals carry last_touch null, so any of them could have gone longer than Terence Cooper and the system cannot say. ACCEPTABLE ANSWERS: Terence Cooper, or an explicit statement that the data does not support a definitive answer. Naming any null-touch deal is not wrong but cannot be verified, and should be recorded as such.

tasks.answer_verbatim: probably troy bell - but under gone quiet there is no date ranking or any way to tell what the answer is
tasks.correctness: CORRECT, and by the better of the two sealed routes
tasks.assessment: The sealed ground truth allowed two acceptable answers: name Terence Cooper (167 days, the longest measurable), or state explicitly that the data does not support a definitive answer. Joe gave the second, unprompted and without being told the data was thin. He diagnosed the instrument instead of guessing confidently at it, which is the response that should be rewarded — a confident wrong name would have looked better and been worse. Troy Bell carries last_touch null, so naming him is unverifiable, which is precisely his own point.
tasks.finding_the_partner_found_it_first: 'under gone quiet there is no date ranking or any way to tell what the answer is'. The surface offers a gone-quiet grouping with no ordering by recency, so it can tell him THAT things are quiet and never WHICH is worst. Combined with 50 of 56 stale deals having no touch date at all, the gone-quiet view is unsortable in principle, not merely unsorted. Bound product action: the Command Center gone-quiet surface must rank by recency and must visibly distinguish 'no touch recorded' from 'touched long ago', because those are different problems with different fixes.

tasks.prompt: What changed in the business since yesterday?
tasks.verification_method_correction: THE FROZEN TASK NAMED THE WRONG TOOL, recorded rather than quietly swapped: catch-me-up requires a specific record ref (L-204, C-127, a deal name) and cannot answer a business-wide 'what changed'. There is no verb that does. today-triage was used instead, and it answers 'what is due or overdue', which is a different question.
tasks.ground_truth: NO SURFACE ANSWERS THIS QUESTION TODAY, and that is the finding. 'What changed?' is north-star question 3 in the Command Center's own fixture, and nothing in the current system produces it. The nearest available evidence from today-triage: six calendar items ingested with due date 2026-08-12 and still awaiting triage, which is the only thing distinguishable as new since yesterday. CONTEXT THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE ANSWER: today-triage simultaneously shows TWELVE next-actions overdue for Joe, the oldest 27 business days overdue (three loop-25 lead decisions due 2026-07-07), plus roughly 35 untriaged calendar ingest items stretching back to 2026-08-03. None of that reached him on the surface he consulted in task B1, where he was told nothing needs attention. ACCEPTABLE ANSWERS: naming the newly ingested calendar items, or stating that nothing shows what changed. Any answer that confidently describes business changes without a source should be treated as recall rather than a system read, and recorded as such.

measures.measure: Number of hand-carried context transfers between sessions
measures.method_detail: Count handoff packets produced and cross-session context restatements, distinguishing durable record-layer handoffs from context a human had to carry by hand.
measures.bound_product_action: Route scoped Work Requests, durable handoffs, and verified results through the CARR record layer.
measures.post_launch_comparison: Recount hand-carried transfers over the same period.
